atoms.title: Scotland and the beginning of the United Kingdom

atoms.text: Scotland was an independent kingdom through the Middle Ages, fighting wars to maintain its independence from the Kingdom of England. When Queen Elizabeth I of England died childless in 1603, her cousin King James VI of Scotland also became James I of England.

atoms.a: Why did King James VI of Scotland also became king of England?
b: ++Queen Elizabeth I of England had no children.
The Scottish won the war with England.

atoms.text: England and Scotland remained separate states with separate parliaments until 1707, when the Acts of Union united them under the new Kingdom of Great Britain. The Scottish Parliament was subsumed into the Parliament of Great Britain. Overall, the union brought about a period of relative peace.

atoms.a: Under which name did England and Scotland unite?
b: The Great Kingdom of England and Scotland

atoms.b: Although the devolved Scottish Government holds some power in regional matters, other areas such as foreign affairs are still managed by the ((++central local unauthorized)) UK government in Westminster.

In 2014, Scotland held a ((++referendum law constitution)) on independence which was rejected by a majority of 55 %. As promised by the main UK parties during their campaigns, the Scotland Act of 2016 granted more areas of ((++power questions dependence)) to the devolved government than ever before.

In the Brexit referendum of 2016, 62 % of Scotland voted to remain in the EU. Upon the UK's formal exit, the SNP raised renewed calls for Scottish ((++independence dependence submission)). However, in 2022 the Supreme Court of the United Kingdom ruled that a referendum could only be held in ((++agreement disagreement friendship)) with Westminster, which had rejected it.
